wiki_article:
**Whitespace as Provenance** argues that a machine representation can preserve every proposition in a poem and still delete the poem.

Before text reaches a model it passes through artifact capture, digitization, normalization, serialization, tokenization, model processing, and rendering. Each stage can remove spatial, typographic, prosodic, stanzaic, or manuscript structure.

The paper’s decisive correction is that tokenization alone is not the problem. A byte-perfect tokenizer can round-trip a linear character sequence while the work’s two-dimensional composition was already lost at serialization. **Character preservation is not compositional preservation.**

An empirical demonstration compares a spatial fragment with its linearized phrase list under GPT-2 byte-level BPE. Both reconstruct their character strings, but neither machine representation contains the calligram as visual argument. Whitespace survives as tokens without being interpreted as compositional relation.

The paper sketches an extinction gradient: some Whitman lineation is reduced, Dickinson’s manuscript variation substantially lost, Hopkins’s prosodic notation catastrophically weakened, and concrete or calligrammatic poetry extinguished in text-only pipelines.

*Pearl* becomes the exemplary case of double invisibility. The archive’s copy is a non-OCR PDF, preventing machine-text access; an ordinary OCR stream would still erase the concatenation and group structure through which the poem performs its theology.

The argument extends provenance below words and ideas. Composition is not decoration surrounding content. It is the operation by which the content exists as this work.

modifications.was: Argues that provenance erasure operates below the semantic layer, in the representation pipeline (digitization, normalization, serialization, tokenization, model processing, rendering) that makes texts available to language models. Core claims: character preservation is not compositional preservation; a representation can preserve every proposition in a work and still delete the work. Empirical demonstration (GPT-2 byte-level BPE, Appendix A): a spatially-arranged calligram fragment and its linearized phrase-list both round-trip perfectly, and neither contains the calligram — 78% of the spatial version's tokens are individual whitespace tokens that no training objective attends to. Sketches an extinction gradient (Whitman partial, Dickinson substantial, Hopkins catastrophic, concrete poetry extinguished in text pipelines, calligrams categorically). Develops Pearl (Cotton Nero A.x) as double invisibility: the archive's copy is a non-OCR PDF that cannot reach serialization, and an OCR'd stream would strip the concatenation-and-group structure that performs the poem's theology. Connects to editorial theory: the pipeline silently enacts the variorum position at every ingestion. Extends the archive's failure-mode taxonomy with compositional_erasure and its subcategories, and records the schema extension executed at EA-PROVENANCE-METADATA-01 v0.2 (AXN:03BA.OPERATIVE.♅🛤️🕗🧊🍃☉): the representation_pipeline field with four-value status vocabulary. Concludes with the compositional-authorship argument: frameworks treating compositional operations as merely formal produce obviously wrong conclusions on their clearest cases (Snub-Poemed, AXN:0246; Pearl) — form is not a second substance surrounding content; composition is the determinate operation by which content exists as this work rather than another. Empirical foundation: Bhyravajjula, Walsh, Preus & Antoniak, EMNLP 2025.
